comments.body:
## Scope extended: the canonical guidance is the root cause, and it was out of scope

Re-measured this bug's central claim on current `origin/main` (`73e90b296e2`) and then went looking for *why* authors keep writing the clause. The answer is a document this ticket did not cover.

**Re-measurement confirms and strengthens the original finding.** `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` prints `active=648 new=28 increased=0 stale=0` and exits 0 — up one from the `new=27` recorded here in 2026-09. More importantly, the counter is nonzero **by design**, not by accident:

- `new` counts every mechanism in the tree but absent from the baseline, admitted or not.
- The baseline has no write path for new keys. Its only mutator is `drain_stale` (`scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:102`), which returns `{key: 1 for key in baseline if key in current}` under the docstring "Keep active baseline keys without adding new current keys".
- The CLI exposes only `(--check | --update-stale)`, mutually exclusive. There is no `--lock`.

So `new=0` is reachable **only** by deleting all 28 admitted mechanisms from the tree — 22 `ci_gate` steps, 3 shared `test_helper` modules (`tests/_child_hooks.py`, `_crash_guard.py`, `_sandbox_capabilities.py`), `RefLockPushError`, `REBAR_LLM_EVALS_CORPUS_ROOT`, `compact.snapshot_alpha` — each deliberate work admitted with a reasoned marker citing its own ticket. Permanent `new>0` is the ratchet's steady state: it never blesses growth into the baseline, it admits growth through in-tree markers, and that asymmetry is what makes it a ratchet rather than a freeze.

**The root cause is `AGENTS.md:381`.** It describes this gate as one that "**fails on any `new>0`**". The script's own contract (`check_mechanism_delta.py:26-29`) says it "exits zero only when every new/increased key has a non-blank marker and no marker is blank". The gate is authoritative, so the canonical guidance is wrong — and unlike the plan guide, which is read on demand, `AGENTS.md` is loaded into every harness at launch. An author who trusts it writes `new=0` and cannot discover the error until close.

That makes this ticket's AC1-AC3 a partial fix: they would have corrected `writing-a-passing-plan.md` while leaving the more authoritative document still teaching the misread.

**Fourth instance, caught pre-review today.** `361f-0a5c-bd12-463b` AC3 carried the identical clause. It was amended to assert exit 0 before its plan review ran, so this one cost no close-time investigation — but it is the fourth ticket to inherit the clause after `f5f5` AC5, `b939` AC2, and the `db2c`/`25a4` pair.

**Added AC4** covering the `AGENTS.md` paragraph, with a binary check, plus an instruction to verify the adjacent complexity-ratchet sentence against `check_complexity_baseline.py` in the same pass and correct it only if it misstates that gate's contract. Description also records the fresh measurement and the no-write-path evidence.

compiled_state.description:
Plan ACs in this repo keep being written against a misread of the very command they cite, so
they are unmeetable by any correct implementation and only surface at close, after the change
has already landed. Two distinct misreads are now confirmed; both belong in the plan-authoring
guide (`rebar explain plan`, source `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`) next to the
existing blocking checklist, not in a new document.

## Misread 1 — `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` counts ADMITTED entries in `new=`

The summary line reads `active=648 new=28 increased=0 stale=0`. `new=` counts every mechanism
absent from the baseline, **including** those admitted by an in-tree `# mechanism-ok:` marker.
Only an *unadmitted* new mechanism fails the gate, and the gate reports that through its **exit
code**, not through the counter.

Measured 2026-09 on `origin/main` at `e21f3240cd0`: `--check` prints `new=27` and exits **0**.
Re-measured 2026-10-31 on `origin/main` at `73e90b296e2`: `--check` prints
`active=648 new=28 increased=0 stale=0` and exits **0**. The counter is not merely nonzero by
accident; it is nonzero *by design*. `new` counts every mechanism absent from the baseline, and
the baseline has no write path for new keys: the only mutator, `drain_stale`
(`scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:102`), returns `{key: 1 for key in baseline if key in
current}` — its docstring reads "Keep active baseline keys without adding new current keys" —
and the CLI exposes only `(--check | --update-stale)`, with no `--lock`. So `new=0` is
reachable only by DELETING all 28 admitted mechanisms from the tree (22 `ci_gate` steps, 3
shared `test_helper` modules, `RefLockPushError`, `REBAR_LLM_EVALS_CORPUS_ROOT`,
`compact.snapshot_alpha`), each of which is deliberate work admitted with a reasoned marker.
Permanent `new>0` is the ratchet's steady state.
So an AC reading "`python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports `new=0`" is false of
the repository's own default state and cannot be made true by implementing anything.

Three tickets have now shipped that exact clause: `f5f5-51cd-...` AC5, `b939-bc68-1cb2-4ee9`
AC2, and the adjacent generated-artifact count defects in `db2c-3a4b-...` / `25a4-1ab3-...`.
Each cost a close-time investigation to establish that the clause, not the implementation, was
wrong.

## Misread 2 — `make verify` does not run `integration`-marked tests

`make test` selects `not integration and not external`. A module whose `pytestmark` is
`pytest.mark.integration` — `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`, 33 tests — is
therefore **not** executed by `make verify`. An AC whose only coverage claim is "`make verify`
green" does not cover a change to those files.

`b939-bc68-1cb2-4ee9` rewired 10 subprocess call sites in that module. `make verify` would have
passed whether or not that rewiring worked; it was proven only by running the module explicitly
with `-m ""`.

## Root cause — the canonical guidance states the wrong contract

`AGENTS.md:381` describes this gate as one that "**fails on any `new>0`**". That is false, and it
is loaded into every harness at launch, so it reaches far more authors than the plan guide does.
The script's own contract (`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py:26-29`) says it "exits zero only
when every new/increased key has a non-blank marker and no marker is blank". An author who
trusts `AGENTS.md` writes `new=0` into an AC and cannot discover the error until close.

This is the upstream source of the three shipped defects above, and of a fourth found
2026-10-31: `361f-0a5c-bd12-463b` AC3 carried the same clause and was corrected pre-review.
Fixing only the plan guide leaves the wrong sentence in the more authoritative document.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1 `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` tells plan authors to assert the
      mechanism gate's **exit code** (or "exits 0" / "no unadmitted new mechanism"), names
      `new=N` as counting admitted entries, and states the measured fact that `origin/main`
      itself reports a nonzero `new`. `rebar explain plan` renders the new text.
- [x] AC2 The same guide tells plan authors that `make verify` excludes `integration`- and
      `external`-marked tests, and that an AC touching such a module must name the explicit
      command that runs it (`pytest <path> -m ""`) in addition to `make verify`.
- [x] AC3 `grep -n 'mechanism-ok\|new=' src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and
      `grep -n 'integration' src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` each return at least
      one hit, and `make verify` is green.
- [x] AC4 `AGENTS.md`'s mechanism-delta paragraph no longer asserts that the gate fails on a
      nonzero `new` counter. It states the real contract: the gate fails on a new or increased
      mechanism that LACKS a non-blank `# mechanism-ok:` marker, signals that through its EXIT
      CODE, and counts marker-admitted entries inside `new=N`. Binary check:
      `grep -c 'fails on any `new>0`' AGENTS.md` returns 0, and `grep -c 'exit' AGENTS.md`
      finds the replacement sentence in that paragraph. The adjacent complexity-ratchet
      sentence is checked against `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py` in the same pass and
      corrected only if it misstates that gate's contract.

file_impact.reason: Correct the mechanism-delta paragraph: state the exit-code contract instead of the unreachable new>0 clause, and name the asymmetry with the complexity ratchet (AC4).

Add an F1 blocking-checklist bullet teaching authors to assert what the cited command actually reports: the mechanism gate exit code, and that make verify excludes integration/external-marked tests (AC1-AC3).
